title: A fixed-point theorem for generalized strictly nonexpansive mappings on bounded sets in complete metric spaces
headline: Open finding: a complete bounded metric space can admit a strictly nonexpansive shift with no fixed point, and a unique fixed point need not attract every orbit.

work.title: A fixed-point theorem for generalized strictly nonexpansive mappings on bounded sets in complete metric spaces

claims.label: Theorem 3.1 and Corollaries 3.2–3.4: fixed-point existence and global convergence
claims.gist: Theorem 3.1 and Corollaries 3.2–3.4 assert fixed-point existence or global convergence under completeness, continuity, bounded-orbit, and strictness conditions.
claims.statement: Under the stated hypotheses, Theorem 3.1 concludes that a unique fixed point exists and every orbit converges to it; Corollaries 3.2–3.4 state corresponding convergence conclusions.
conditions: The self-map is continuous and satisfies the strict condition in definition (1.7) for every distinct pair.
Theorem 3.1 assumes at least one bounded orbit; Corollaries 3.2–3.4 have their stated fixed-point or bounded-closed-set hypotheses.
claims.quantifiers: The stated existence and global-convergence conclusions apply to every map and space satisfying the respective theorem or corollary hypotheses.

result.summary: The explicit complete bounded metric shift refutes the stated existence conclusion; adjoining a fixed point refutes global convergence while conditional uniqueness survives.
result.witness: For positive integers n, let a(n)=1/n and d(u,v)=0 if u=v, otherwise 1+|a(u)-a(v)|. This is bounded and complete. T(n)=n+1 strictly reduces every distinct pair's distance but has no fixed point. Add p with a(p)=0, set T(p)=p, and keep T(n)=n+1. Then p is the unique fixed point while d(T^k n,p)=1+1/(n+k) tends to 1 instead of 0.
result.argument: For n<m, d(Tn,Tm)=1+(m-n)/((n+1)(m+1)) < 1+(m-n)/(nm)=d(n,m). The shift satisfies the strictness assumption on the whole complete bounded space while failing existence. The adjoined-point construction preserves strictness and has a unique fixed point, but its orbit distances converge to 1. Conditional uniqueness remains valid.
not_claimed: Conditional uniqueness of a fixed point remains valid.
The counterexamples do not establish that every result in the article is false.
result.repair_note: Additional hypotheses would need to rule out bounded 1-separated orbits and justify the convergence step; a repaired theorem is not established here.
